proof.criterion: Review round 2 finding A: every graceful hand-over, not only the first, delivers within 10 s (3 s hold)
proof.surface: real cmd/listener processes built at 9c5cd05b for machine box-smoke, each signed in with box-smoke's nkey under the rendered ListenerPermissions grant, against a real nats-server 2.10.29 process; a fake serving port (204, 500 for a failing session, never answers a prompt in hand); sends via /v1/messages/send
proof.command: python3 $TMPDIR/infra557-test/roll.py $TMPDIR/infra557-test/listener-head8 h8-roll roll (graceful stops A->B->C->D, each a second into a prompt in hand, a failing session's 30 s retry outstanding, a send every 100 ms to two healthy sessions)
proof.observed: hand-overs 3.58 / 3.80 / 3.55 s; 257 messages, 0 missing, 0 repeats, slowest 7.60 s, 0 later than 10 s, each session in order, 0 permission violations (the run before the drain gave 7.57 s too)
proof.negativeControl: the same run with a binary built at 75ad2486: slowest 11.09 s, 12 messages later than 10 s

proof.criterion: Review round 2 finding A after a node loss: every graceful hand-over delivers within 10 s
proof.surface: as above; the active pod SIGSTOPped (its connections stay open, as on a lost node), then the pod that took its expired lease and each later holder stopped gracefully
proof.observed: pod-b took the frozen pod's lease after 4.9 s; hand-overs 3.55 / 3.54 s; 183 messages, 0 missing, 0 repeats, slowest 7.55 s, 0 later than 10 s, each session in order
proof.negativeControl: the same run at 75ad2486: slowest 11.59 s, 33 messages later than 10 s

proof.criterion: Review round 2 finding B: a hard take-over by a pod that gave the lease up while waiting out a binding keeps its settle hold and per-session order
proof.surface: real processes under the rendered grant on a real nats-server 2.10.29: a pre-lease build (main 571f729b) binds the durable; pod-x (nkey box-x, box-smoke's grant) takes the lease and waits the binding out; a config reload (SIGHUP) drops box-x's CONSUMER.INFO/CREATE for the durable; pod-y (nkey box-smoke) takes over; the grant is restored and the old build stops; pod-y prompts 'older', which is never answered, and is SIGSTOPped; 30 'newer' sends follow, one every 200 ms
proof.observed: pod-x logged ERROR 'lease holder cannot deliver from the durable' 143 s after the reload and gave the lease up; pod-y took it. After the freeze, pod-x took the expired lease (settle true), logged 'term must settle', and the settle hold ended after 6.0 s (outcome settled, 31 messages). The session took older, newer-1 ... newer-30 in publish order, the last 11.16 s after the freeze
proof.negativeControl: the same run at 75ad2486: pod-x took the expired lease, logged 'durable is push-bound by a subscriber without the lease; waiting for its binding to end', and delivered nothing within 60 s

observations: A SIGKILL form of the finding-B run kept order at both heads: the dead pod's message was back before the take-over, so that form cannot tell the heads apart. The frozen-node form above is deterministic and is the one recorded.
The multiprocess run was made on the pod before the 10:08Z drain. The real-surface runs were repeated on the new pod after the resume, at the same code head.
